question.text: A client wants to start a monthly SIP of Rs. 5,000 across three different AMCs. The distributor suggests using MF Utilities (MFU). Why is this recommendation appropriate?

answer.text: MFU offers higher returns on SIP investments compared to investing directly with AMCs
MFU automatically waives all SEBI-mandated charges on SIP investments
MFU allows the client to use a single Common Transaction Form and make one consolidated payment for SIPs across all three AMCs through a Common Account Number (CAN)
MFU guarantees that SIP installments will never miss due to its automated debit system

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.119), MF Utilities (MFU) provides investors with a Common Account Number (CAN), a Common Transaction Form usable across participating mutual funds, multiple payment modes, and the ability to make a single consolidated payment for multiple subscriptions. For a client running SIPs across three AMCs, this means one form, one CAN, and one consolidated payment instead of three separate workflows. The Trap: Option A is wrong — MFU is a transaction infrastructure platform, not a return-enhancing product. Option D overpromises — MFU facilitates transactions but cannot guarantee that bank debits will always succeed. Note: Per p.127, the earlier transaction-charge framework that applied above the Rs.10,000 threshold has been withdrawn under the August 2025 SEBI circular, so distractors based on that rule are no longer current.
